chunks: A number of our companions, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Khalid, from Amr ibn Uthman, from Muhammad ibn Salim al-Kindi, from the one who narrated to him, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said:

The Commander of the Faithful (peace be upon him) used to say whenever he ascended the pulpit: 'It is befitting for the Muslim to avoid establishing brotherhood with three types: the shameless immoral, the fool, and the liar.'

As for the shameless immoral one, he beautifies his deed for you and desires that you be like him, and he does not assist you in the matters of your religion and your Hereafter; his closeness is aversion and harshness, and his coming and going is a disgrace upon you.

And as for the fool, he gives you no good counsel, nor can he be relied upon to repel harm from you, even if he exerted himself; and sometimes when he intends your benefit, he ends up harming you. Thus his death is better than his life, his silence is better than his speech, and his distance is better than his nearness.

And as for the liar, life with him brings you no ease: he spreads your words to others and brings others' words to you; every time he exhausts a tale, he pours out another like it, until even when he speaks truthfully, he is not believed, and he sows division among people through enmity, cultivating hatred in their hearts.
So fear God, Mighty and Majestic, and look out for yourselves.

key_terms.السَّخَائِمُ: Rancour/hatred — deep-seated hatred or malice lodged in the heart
key_terms.الْأَحْمَقُ: The fool/idiot — not merely unintelligent, but one whose poor judgment makes him dangerous even when well-intentioned
key_terms.الْكَذَّابُ: The habitual liar — one whose chronic dishonesty eventually destroys their credibility even when telling the truth, and spreads discord
key_terms.الْمَاجِنُ الْفَاجِرُ: The shameless and immoral person — one who publicly disregards moral boundaries and actively tries to normalize vice in others
key_terms.مَعَادِكَ: Your Hereafter/return to God — the afterlife and final accounting
key_terms.مُوَاخَاةَ: Brotherhood/fraternization — in early Islamic society, a formal bond of mutual support and solidarity, not mere casual friendship

ai.seo_question: What types of companions did Imam Ali warn Muslims to avoid?
ai.summary: This hadith preserves a sermon that Imam Ali (AS) regularly delivered from the pulpit, reported through Imam al-Sadiq (AS). Imam Ali warns Muslims against three types of destructive companions: the dissolute libertine who normalizes sin, the fool who harms despite good intentions, and the habitual liar whose falsehoods destroy trust and sow enmity. The exhortation concludes with a call to God-consciousness (taqwa), situating social ethics within a framework of divine accountability. The original audience — early Muslims navigating communal life in the expanding Islamic polity — would have understood 'brotherhood' (muwa'akhah) as a formal bond of mutual responsibility, making this warning about its misuse especially weighty.
